1.note: The Rav Safra and R. Abbahu anecdote is usually located in b. Avodah Zarah 4a. The author's attribution to Helek is kept.

2.note: In Herodotus (Book I) Tomyris is queen of the Massagetae, a Scythian people; the author's 'Shitim' is translated as Scythians.

3.note: The figure 17 Nisan is kept as printed; the aim stated is that the festival falls in the proper (spring) season.

4.note: The author attributes Sha'ar ha-Shamayim to Isaac Israeli; the work of that title usually cited is by Gershon b. Solomon. The attribution is kept and not resolved here.

5.note: The identity of this R. Maimon, author of a commentary on al-Farghani, is uncertain. The name is transliterated.

6.note: An anonymous commentator on Maimonides' Hilkhot Kiddush ha-Hodesh, not further identified.

7.he: וי"ד וג"י תת"עו ... ז"ט תרמ"ב וד"ט תרמ"ב
7.note: These calendrical signs are transliterated as given (days-hours-parts). Their exact values are not resolved here.

8.note: The Temples were destroyed in Av, the eleventh month counting from Tishri; the text's 'tenth' may reflect a different count. Kept as written.

9.note: The six-month reign in 2 Kgs 15:8 is Zechariah's, not Ahaziah's; the text reads Ahaziah. Kept as written.

10.note: Identification of this commentator on aggadot is uncertain; the name is transliterated.

11.note: Adding 2d 4h 438p to BaHaRaD (2d 5h 204p) gives 4d 9h 642p (the molad of Nisan, as in segment 141). The printed ז (7) for the day is kept. The sense of 'the days of its rebuke' is not explained in this chapter.

12.note: Arithmetically, 6d 14h + 4d 8h 876p gives 3d 22h 876p; the printed figure is kept. The same applies in segments 114-115.

13.note: The attribution and exact wording of this dictum are uncertain.

14.note: It is unclear which work entitled Sha'ar ha-Shamayim is meant; the 'I' who proved the point in Yesod Olam suggests the author is Isaac Israeli. The title is transliterated.

15.he: ר' חסאן הדיין ור' יצחק בן רקופאל
15.note: Names transliterated as printed; the identification of Ben Rakufal is uncertain.

16.note: Subtracting one cycle (2-16-595) from BaHaRaD (2-5-204) arithmetically gives 6-12-689, not 4-21-799; the figure is kept as printed and the intended calculation is unclear.

17.note: Read as 11 days and 204 parts (i.e. the solar-lunar excess); the abbreviation is obscure in the printing.

18.note: Transliterated; the identification of this Christian author on calendar reform is uncertain.

19.note: Same unidentified author as in segment 117.
